title: CLR/22/2025 of RAKESH BHARDWAJ Vs ANIL GIRI

COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
CLR/22/2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for
the revisionist.
2. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned
counsel for the respondent.
3. The instant civil revision has been
preferred by the revisionist against the
judgment and order dated 07.02.2025,
passed by learned Judge SCC/ Ist
Additional District Judge, Haridwar in
SCC Suit Case No. 05 of 2021, Sri Anil
Giri vs. Sri Rakesh Bhardwaj, whereby
the suit for eviction/recovery of rent and
damages has been decreed.
4. Mr. Arpit Bhardwaj, power of
attorney holder of Mr. Rakesh Bhardwaj
(father)/ revisionist and the respondent/
plaintiff Anil Giri are present in Court.
5. On several dates, the matter was
heard at length. However, today both Mr.
Arpit Bhardwaj, power of attorney holder
of Mr. Rakesh Bhardwaj (father)/
revisionist and Mr. Anil Giri who are
present in Court submits that they come
up with the settlement that the
revisionist shall vacate the shop in
question within two years from today,
i.e. on or before 30.11.2027.
5. Both the parties are identified by
their respective counsel. Xerox copy of
the Aadhar cards, signed by the parties
and verified by their counsel are filed
and kept on record.
6. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, who appears
for the respondent submits that since the
respondent/plaintiff is himself present in
Court and agrees with the proposal,
therefore, revision may be disposed of in
terms of the aforesaid settlement arrived
in between the parties.

2025:UHC:10398
7. In view of the statement, as made
above, and undertaking as given by Arpit
Bhardwaj, power of attorney holder of
Mr. Rakesh Bhardwaj (father) the instant
civil revision is disposed of finally with
the direction to the revisionist to vacate
the shop in question on or before
30.11.2027 and shall pay monthly rent
regularly, as agreed.
8. It is made clear that if the
revisionist fails to vacate the shop in
question on or before 30.11.2027, the
Executing Court shall immediately take
steps against the revisionist.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
21.11.2025
Parul
